title: Priv VPC IAM: least-privilege starter kit + migration adapter
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Build a reusable Terraform module (tf module + upgrade adapter) that provides a minimal, auditable RBAC/IAM surface for Private (VPC) deployments. The module should make it easy to (1) create least-privilege roles and role bindings for common Redwood components, (2) generate machine-friendly role manifests for customers, and (3) provide a migration shim for existing deployments that use older permissive policies.

Goals: Provide an opinionated default that reduces blast radius, ship a migration path for customers with permissive policies, include runtime health checks and IAM drift detection hooks, and produce human- and machine-readable policy artifacts for audits. Module must support AWS primarily (IAM + STS + condition keys) and be extensible to GCP/Azure in a follow-up.

Constraints & non-goals: This ticket does not rework the Console UI or RBAC UX. It does not include a managed orchestration plane — the module is IaC only. We will not attempt to fully auto-rewrite existing customer policies; we provide a guided migration tool and audit reports instead.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable Terraform module is published under modules/priv-iam-starter with clear inputs/outputs and examples
Module creates documented IAM roles for core components: api-server, inference-worker, metrics-writer, log-uploader, and admin-breakglass
Generated policies default to least-privilege (deny by default, allow specific actions) and include optional allowlists for customer-provided ARNs
Migration adapter can scan an existing IAM policy (via provided data source) and produce a report mapping permissive statements to least-privilege recommendations
Integration tests run in CI that validate role assumption (STS:AssumeRole) and basic policy simulator checks using AWS IAM Access Analyzer or policy-sim stub
Module emits Terraform outputs and an artifacts JSON file suitable for inclusion in audits (roles.json, recommendations.md)
Security review sign-off recorded and an automated drift detection plan added to Ops playbooks
tasks: Define module surface: inputs (environment, prefix, customer_allowlist, admin_principals), outputs (role_arns, policy_documents, artifacts_path)
Author HCL for roles + policy documents using templatefile to keep statements clear
Add data sources to fetch existing policies and produce migration report (dry-run only)
Implement optional breakglass role with KMS-wrapped access key rotation guidance
Write integration tests: terraform apply -> assume role -> call STS GetCallerIdentity -> assert expected permissions
Add CI job that runs acceptance tests against a sandbox AWS account and publishes artifacts
Document upgrade path: from legacy permissive module to starter kit with migration adapter and rollout canary guidance
rollout_plan: Week 0: Merge module to mono-repo 'modules/priv-iam-starter' behind feature flag
Week 1: Run CI integration tests and internal dogfooding on sandbox account (team infra)
Week 2: Create migration reports for two pilot customers (with permission) and validate no service interruption in canary
Week 3: Publish docs and example configs in the private-deploy repo; request security review
Week 4: Offer module in Solutions catalog and announce to customers with migration checklist
notes: Design decisions: prefer explicit policy statements vs large wildcard statements. Use condition keys (aws:SourceVpc, aws:SourceIp) where applicable to bind roles to VPC boundaries.
Trade-offs: Tight policies will require more initial work to enumerate allowed S3 prefixes, KMS keys and ECR repos. To lower friction we provide a 'discovery' CLI to suggest allowlists.

Testing approach: Use a short-lived sandbox AWS account for CI; tests should not rely on long-lived credentials. We will stub Access Analyzer in unit tests and run full policy-sim in integration only.

migration_notes: Migration adapter overview: run 'tfplan_scan' (thin wrapper) to export existing policy statements. Adapter maps broad actions (s3:*, kms:*) to recommended granular actions and suggests resource ARNs. Output: roles.json + recommendations.md. Migration is non-destructive by default; we provide a 2-step apply: deploy shim 'legacy-allowlist' that mirrors old policy in a single managed role, then replace consumers one-by-one with least-privilege roles using canary traffic routing.
test_matrix: Integration tests: assume-role, get-caller-identity, put-object(s3 only to allowed prefix), describe-db, publish-metric. Unit tests: template rendering, policy lint, policy-sim stubs. CI matrix includes Terraform 1.4.x and 1.5.x.
